GC200.status: Classical result established; withdraw open-problem classification
GC200.model: Let \(T=\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R/L_y\mathbb Z\), \(L_x,L_y>0\), and \(u\in H^1(T;S^1)\) with winding \((m,n)\in\mathbb Z^2\). Minimize \(E(u)=\frac12\int_T|\nabla u|^2\).
GC200.canonical: The exact answer is \(\min_{[u]=(m,n)}E(u)=2\pi^2(m^2L_y/L_x+n^2L_x/L_y)\). Every fixed-winding representative admits \(u=e^{i[2\pi(mx/L_x+ny/L_y)+f]}\) with periodic real \(f\in H^1(T)\); integration removes the affine-gradient cross term, yielding \(E(u)=E_{\min}+\frac12\int_T|\nabla f|^2\). Minimizers are the harmonic phase representatives, unique up to a constant phase.
GC200.resolution: The stated analytic target is settled by this elementary Hodge/harmonic phase calculation. For an exact Lean completion, formalize winding decomposition, periodic integration and the energy identity; any new dynamics question must introduce a separate evolution equation.
